---
title: "Train and reuse your first surrogate"
execute:
  eval: false
---

This example uses a bundled SIRDS simulation bank: 100 parameter groups, five
replicates and 40 timepoints. It checks the complete workflow on a CPU.
A short run is not a scientifically validated epidemic surrogate.

## Install

Use Python 3.11 or newer in an isolated environment. The following chooses
CPU PyTorch. For CUDA, install the PyTorch build appropriate to your hardware.

```bash
python -m pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
python -m pip install "metis-surrogate @ git+https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git"
metis demo --steps 100 --output metis-demo
```

This creates `model.pt`, `metrics.json` and `prediction.npy`. `model.pt` includes
preprocessing and the ordered input/output schema, so it can be moved to a
machine that does not have the original bank. The package is not yet on PyPI;
the existing `metis` PyPI project is unrelated.

## Train in Python

```{python}
from metis import load_example, Surrogate, TrainingConfig

bank = load_example()
split = bank.split(validation_fraction=0.2, test_fraction=0.2, seed=42)
model = Surrogate("mlp").fit(
    split.train,
    validation=split.validation,
    config=TrainingConfig(steps=500, device="cpu"),
)
report = model.evaluate(split.test)
print(report.by_output)
print(report.worst_groups(5))
model.save("surrogate.pt")
report.save("evaluation.json")
```

A step is an optimizer update, not a full pass through the bank. Validation
chooses the best evaluated model weights. The test set does not influence
scaling, optimization or weight selection. Reserve it for assessing a final
choice; a sweep should use validation for model comparison and assess test
performance only after the choice is made.

## Reload and predict

```{python}
restored = Surrogate.load("surrogate.pt")
prediction = restored.predict({
    "I_0": 0.04, "beta": 0.4, "gamma": 0.15, "omega": 0.02, "mu": 0.02
})
print(prediction.shape)  # (1, 40, 4), original compartment-count units
```

A dict names the inputs; arrays must follow `restored.input_names`. The time grid
and output order are `restored.times` and `restored.output_names`. Extrapolating
outside the training input ranges emits a warning rather than clipping values.

## Use Hydra instead

```bash
metis train model=mlp training.steps=500 training.device=cpu
```

This calls the same `Surrogate.fit` and evaluation methods. Hydra adds
configuration composition, run directories, overrides and sweeps.
See [the Hydra workflow](hydra.qmd).
